titleStmt.title: Interview with Archie L. Smith, Undated
titleStmt.author: Bonita Callahan

projectDesc.p: Encoded for the Experiencing War web site for the Veterans History Project.

samplingDecl.p: The recording of the interview with Archie L. Smith was digitized.

editorialDecl.p: This transcription was encoded with minimal changes to the original text in an effort to preserve original content and idiosyncrasies of the person interviewed. Period language and terminology are also retained. Encoding is literal with regard to the transcriptionist's capitalization, punctuation, and spelling. Spelling errors are indicated with [sic]; however, recurring errors in spelling within a single document have been marked the first time and not subsequently.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Bonita Callahan. I am interviewing Archie L. Smith in his home, who was a former member of the Marine Corps. I am a member of the DAR and of the Francis Slocum chapter of Wabash, Indiana. Mr. Smith, you enlisted in the Marine Corps, and that was in?

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: After you had graduated from high school?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, why did you select the Marine Corps?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Because my stepfather was a Marine, and I just liked it.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: At that particular time, you were living where?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Saginaw, Michigan.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: From -- from your time of enlistment, you went to San Diego?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: San Diego.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: San Diego.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I had to go to Chicago first and then they sent me to San Diego.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And did you think the training was difficult?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I thought it was very good and hard but not difficult.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: From there after your boot training, you were placed on a battleship?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes, on the U.S.S. Nevada.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And that was one that was at Pearl Harbor?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: It was in at Pearl Harbor.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: You were traveling in the Pacific for approximately two and a half years?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And one of the things you experienced was searching for Amelia Earhart?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Went out and search -- when her plane crashed someplace out there, they thought we went out looking for her, we could find her, but we didn't.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, after that, you went to San Diego -- you returned to San Diego?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Returned to San Diego.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And at that particular time, you were in the artillery unit?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And that was about 1940?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: About that.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, at that particular time when you were on leave, you became -- you were married in 1940?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I married in 1940.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Alrighty. And then you decided to retire?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And so you were in the Marine Reserve?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: For a very short time?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Well, I wasn't retired. I just did not reenlist, because I couldn't. I just quit, but I had to stay in the Reserves.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: So you had really enlisted for four years?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: All right. And then you reenlisted again, and that was in April of '42?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I think that is correct.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And after your second enlistment, you went to Philadelphia?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And there you were in the Naval yards?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And you were working as guard duty --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Guard duty.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- for a very short time?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Then you went to Virginia to a Marine base?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Quantico, Virginia

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Quantico, Virginia. And there you taught a Marine Transport School?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Motor Transport School.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Alrighty. And those were -- what kind of vehicles, were they, could you tell us?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Trucks.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Trucks. And you had several different kinds, you said?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Oh, yes. Well, mostly ours were all International.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Alrighty.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: We had a few jeeps, something like that, but the schooling was on International trucks.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Do you -- then from there you went back to Camp Lejeune --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- in North Carolina, and you became a supply man?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Finally, I became a supply man.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And did you -- you went back on board ship and ended up in Guadal Canal?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Guadal Canal.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, tell me a little bit about Guadal Canal.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Guadal Canal was not a very good place. It -- a lot of fighting there. It was a very unpleasant island, I thought, because we weren't used to it. It was all -- the natives were nice people, but it was a big pineapple plantation for some company. I don't remember who it was.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, there was still some Japs around?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: There was still some around, still some Japanese forces. Finally, we got them all run off, and they were in another area. I don't know where they were, but we were there waiting to go someplace else after that all finished.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, at that particular time, you were still working with the trucks?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And the supplies?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: All right. Your next place, you went to Okinawa?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Went to Okinawa.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And you were involved in the ____ --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Made the initial landing in Okinawa.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: In the invasion, and at that particular time you had what type of vehicle? The am- --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Amphibious trucks.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: All right. Do you know -- can you remember anything about the actual landing in combat?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: The landing wasn't the best. It was -- Iowa lost two ducks going in, two amphibian trucks. But I was very fortunate, I didn't lose any men until after we got on -- on the landing.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Uh-hum.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: But it was not a very pleasant situation.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Uh-hum. And were you injured or -- at all?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: No, I came awful close, but fortunately I did not.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: You were lucky?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I was lucky. I just had my short collar shot off.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Your shirt collar?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: The back of my shirt --

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: That was pretty close.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: That was close.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: After that, do you remember how long you stayed in Okinawa?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Until it was finished, until they secured Okinawa.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Was it several months?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I just really don't know. It was several months, yes. I know that. But --

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And from there you went to Guam?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: No, went back to -- yeah, back to Guam to reorganize.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: You reorganized?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: To get ready for the landing in Japan.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And you thought that you were going to do the --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Japan.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- amphibious --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes, amphibious landing --

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- landing?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: -- in Japan.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: But what saved you?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: The war ended.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: So peace was declared?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And you said that you were ready to invade Japan and you had 52 new vehicles?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: 52 new vehicles.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: All ready?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: All ready.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Uh-hum. And then you did not return home; you went on to China?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Went to China. (Ensign) with General Shepherd.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And do you remember anything about that? What happened? What did you do?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Well, we were there to make sure that everything was taken care of as far as the war was ended. The Japanese forces were in the area and they were -- General Shepherd had made an agreement with them on their surrender, and then we were there as occupational forces to make sure that everything was going right. And I visited a couple, a Japanese family, a husband and wife. Very enjoyable people.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: You didn't speak Japan --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: No, I did not speak their language, but we got along.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: All right. And then -- we are now at 1946 sometime, and you were returned to San Francisco?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: You were then sent back to, or did you -- were finished with your tour of duty or you were just sent back to Indianapolis?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Well, my time was up. My tour of duty was up, and they sent me back to -- back to Indianapolis, yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And, again, you were working for Standard Oil?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Standard Oil Company of Indiana.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Okay. But now this was in '46, early in '46. In June of '46, you were able -- you and your wife were able to adopt a son.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And she was an RN?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: She was an RN.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Working in the --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Indianap- -- Indiana -- Indianapolis -- the Indiana University --

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: School of Nursing?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: -- Medical Center.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And but then, again, you reenlisted?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Reenlisted.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And you thought it was sometime in late summer or fall of '46?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And where were you then? Where were you sent?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Sent back to Washington, D.C.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And you had a reason for going there. You were going to write a book?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I went there -- this officer friend of mine got me there on a -- to write a book on the supplies and --

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Of the Marine Corps?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Of the Marine Corps, on vehicle supplies, automotive work.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Uh-hum. And do you know how long that took you to finish the book?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I was there working on that book about two and a half to three years, I'm sure.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Uh-hum. Uh-hum. And at the same time your wife and child were nearby?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: They -- we were living in Alexandria, Virginia.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, at that particular time, or sometime in that area, you were promoted to warrant officer?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: No, it was after I left Washington, D.C., and after I got down in Virginia, down in North Carolina.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: So, then, after you finished the book, you were made a warrant officer. And one of the things while you were in the Washington, D.C., area, was you saw the inaugural or heard the inauguration of -- would you tell us.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: We went over to Washington, D.C., to watch it over there, the inauguration of Harry Truman.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And that was his --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Second.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: When he was elected?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yeah, yeah, right.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: All right. Can you tell us anything about it?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Well, it was quite a parade, I know that. But an awful lot of people.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, was your son able to be there, too?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: We took him. He was just little, but we took him along.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: All right. Now, you are back in Camp Lejeune, and this is about 1952?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And you are supply officer?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And from there, the Korean operation --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Korean situation.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Yes. And you were in Japan and Korea, again as supply officer?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: But several times you went to Japan?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I was in -- actually in Japan three times.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: All right. Can you tell us anything about your experience there.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Well, some things I did, I can't talk about, because we were in secret stuff, secret things, another man and I, another warrant officer and I, but we enjoyed it. We were a supply group for -- following the Marines in the area, in the Pacific. And then I had a secretary, a little Japanese girl. I thought she was very, very nice. And I called her Skoshi (ph). I didn't -- I couldn't pronounce her full name, but I got acquainted with her, and I went with her to visit where her father -- where they have stuff for her father. He was killed by the atomic bomb in Hiroshima, and I went with to this island with her to see how she did for her father, which she went through a big process. They have quite a thing over there, their process. They go through different stations and they do the talking and so forth.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Of the burial?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: No, this was -- the burial, there was no place there to bury anybody. But on -- they had a -- I'm not sure what they called it, but an area where you went through different stations about the dead people of your family.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Uh-hum.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: And it was like having prayer and so forth, and they did certain things at a different station, and it was -- it was quite an experience.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, you also visited her home with her mother and grandmother?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Her mother, grandmother and her younger sister, I visited with them, and I had meals with them and they accepted me. And we -- we had a very nice time. In fact, they sent my wife a real fancy dress, the Japanese kimona and everything to go with it, so -- so it was something.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And they felt no resentment because --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- because of the Americans?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: No, not at all.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: That was good. So you were in Japan several times, and during that time -- and this is about in '52 and '53 -- and you thought you were there about a year?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: The best I can remember, a year, a little over a year.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, during that time, you went back to Camp Lejeune, and that is when you decided that you were going to retire?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Retire and --

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And this is nine --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: -- become a minister.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And you decided to become a minister, and you attended the seminary. Can you tell us where?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: The Prebysterian Seminary of -- in Decatur, Ala- -- or Decatur, Georgia, Columbia Theological Seminary.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, about that same time, your son had finished high school?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: He finished high school while we lived there in Georgia, and then he decided he wanted to join the Marine Corps, so I, as a chief warrant officer, I got to bring him -- get him into the Marine Corps.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And he was in the Marines for?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: About six years.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Uh-huh. And then he came back to Indiana?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Then he came back to Indiana, and instead of reenlisting, he decided to become a state trooper.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And now where is he now? He has retired from the --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: He has retired from the state police, and he is living in our house up at Orland, Indiana, off Wall Lake out of Orland.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: At that particular time when he served as a state policeman, he was in the toll road area?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yeah, he ran the toll road.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Uh-hum. Now, after you graduated from the seminary, you -- your first parsonage was in Georgia?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Fitzgerald, Georgia.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And you were there about four to five years?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Okay. And then you visited friends in Indiana?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Friends in Indiana.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And can you tell us what happened.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Well, there was -- my wife's sister, we went to visit them, and it was on a weekend. And they -- we wanted to go to church. So she said, "Well, let's stop here at the Hopewell Presbyterian Church." And I said, "Well, they don't have a minister; let's go into town." And she said, "Oh, no, this man's pretty good." So that's where we went to church.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And then what happened?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Well, we got to talking, and they asked me, since I was a minister, if I would have the next Sunday for them since they didn't have a minister. So I preached for them the next Sunday, and then later on they asked me if I would come and be their minister.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: While you were in Georgia, they asked you to come to Franklin --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- Indiana, to be their minister?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And it took you about six months before you arranged that?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes. Well, I had to -- since I had preached there, I had to wait so long before anything could happen.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Since you had preached in Georgia?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yeah -- no, since I preached at Hopewell. See, then I had to wait so long, according to the Presbyterian Church then. That was the Old Synods of Indiana.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: I see. So you were just following the Presbyterian rules?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And then you were at Franklin as a pastor for --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- about four years, you think?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: About that.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And then you were the Presbytry?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yeah.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: That's the ruling body of the Presbyterian Church.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I was --

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: I'll ask you to do something else, and you tell us.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Overseas some retirement homes that the Synods of Indiana had at that time, one in Greenwood, one in Indianapolis, one in Muncie, one in West Lafayette, one in Bloomington, Illinois, and one down in Albany, Georgia -- or Albany, Indiana.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: But then in 1980 you retire -- decided to retire?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: However, you went to Franklin, Indiana?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: You lived there, but you didn't completely retire? Won't you --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Wait a minute. Oh, yes, went to Franklin.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: You retired at --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- Franklin, Indiana? And then you were called to Alabama to preach?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Well, yes, but that was -- I'm trying to think of the name of the town. Troy, Alabama.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Troy and --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: At a church there, and so I went down, and I stayed there for two and a half or three years. I'm not sure just exactly how long it was, and then I came back to Indiana.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And in 1991 is when you came to Peabody Retirement Community?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: That's right. I retired and came --

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: You and your wife?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Right.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Okay. Now, unfortunately your wife was not well, and she expired several years --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Oh, she was very well. She died suddenly and unexpectedly.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Okay. And what -- do you remember when?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: On September the 5th, 1997.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Okay. And you have been here since?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, I need to ask you some questions about your time of service. Did you receive any metals or citations?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Nothing other than normal.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Normal. So you have that. How did you feel about the branch of the service that you joined? You still respected and admired the officers?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Oh, yes. Things have changed since I was in, but it's still -- yes, very much so.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: You always had plenty of supplies?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And you said the food, you accepted it?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Sure. There was nothing you could do except make the best of it.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, did you carry a good luck charm?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: No, ma'am.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And the entertainment, you said that was nonexisting because you were moving all the time?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Nonexistent. We were on the road, moving all the time.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Uh-huh. And the GI Bill, you took advantage of it when you went to the seminary?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: All right. And you had one good friend, the captain, that you kept in contact with --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- for many years?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes, that's right.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Do you want to give his name?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Perry Hargraves.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And after he died, you kept in contact --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: With his wife

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- with his wife? Very good. At the present time, you belong to a --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: The Retirement Officers Association.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: And that is for all officers --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: All officers.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- of all branches?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Of all military branches.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Okay. Now, what do you think about war, and what are your feelings about it?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Well, I feel definitely that war can be presented if everyone will get together and talk and come to an agreement. Of course, we don't all like to agree on the same thing, but I think it's possible for these things to happen, even though they don't.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Right. Now, how did you think your service and experience affected your life?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Oh, I think it did real good. It gave me a view of things that I wouldn't ordinarily know about. If you never been in the military, there are a lot of things you don't realize and don't know about that are just normal.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Now, you had about 24 years of service in the Marines --

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: -- with your three times of enlistment?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: Yes.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Do you think that the experience in the service had something to do with your bringing into the ministry?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: I'm sure it did, because I was involved with a minister in North Carolina that brought me to a lot of light. And he was real helpful and he -- I think I saw the light of God, and I think this helped a whole lot. This is what really got me started.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Is there anything else you would like to say, or have we missed anything that you'd like to add?

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: No, but then to go on back farther, of course, I was involved with the church when I was a teenager in Elwood with my family --

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Uh-hum.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: -- my mother and father, and we all went to church there. And I was very much involved in the youth group, but in the Marine Corps, I kind of got away from it until I finally saw the light, and I came back in.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Very good. Now, we call him Leon here at Peabody, and I do thank you for your time and for your narrations that you have given me, and I am sure that other people will enjoy it, too. Thank you.

sp.speaker: Archie L. Smith
sp.p: It is been my pleasure.

sp.speaker: Bonita Callahan
sp.p: Thank you.
[CONCLUSION OF INTERVIEW]
